fields.summary: Conduit — accounts, articles, comments, favourites and discovery

content.text: Conduit is our public writing platform (web app + JSON API; the contract follows the RealWorld specification — see
). This story is the acceptance baseline for the platform's core: accounts, publishing, commenting, favouriting, following and discovering articles.
: any reader, signed in or not, must be able to discover and read any author's articles and the comments on them.
, I want to publish, edit and delete my articles, so that I control my content.
, I want to discover articles by author and tag, read comments and favourite articles, so that I can follow what interests me.
, I want predictable errors and safe retries, so that client apps behave consistently.

: Favouriting is idempotent: favouriting an article increases
(e.g. a double-click or retry) leaves the count unchanged; unfavouriting decreases it by one.
: A registered user can sign in on the web app's Sign in page with email and password; afterwards the navigation shows their username and a "New Article" link.
: A signed-in writer can publish an article from the editor ("New Article"); the article page then shows the title and body, and the article is available from the API under its slug.
: An anonymous visitor sees "Sign in" and "Sign up" links in the navigation.

7 application defect(s) reproduced by the evaluator: the AUT does not satisfy AC-3, AC-6, AC-10, AC-11, AC-14, AC-15, AC-16. Awaiting reviewer confirmation.
Other readers cannot find an author's articles by ?author=
Comments are visible only to the commenter
Wrong password is answered 403 instead of 401
Second article with the same title is rejected (422 must be unique)
Favouriting is not idempotent (second favourite counts again)
limit outside 1–100 is accepted instead of 422
Deleting someone else's comment answers 404 instead of 403
Each finding in the attached report has reproduction steps (manual, curl and automated re-run), evidence and a reviewer-decision checkbox. No issues were raised automatically.
G5 — what status should an invalid offset (negative or non-numeric) return? The contract only says "offset (≥ 0)". Not tested.
